recommendations.name: Tomato
recommendations.reason: Your family loves tacos and salads, so growing tomatoes will give you fresh salsa and salad toppings, saving $102.

recommendations.name: Green Onion
recommendations.reason: Your tacos and omelets need green onions, and they grow easily in a small space, saving $23.
recommendations.season_note: Comfortably fits your ~314-day season, with room for a second sowing.

recommendations.name: Spinach

crops.name: Acorn Squash
crops.description: Compact winter squash; one fruit is a dinner for two.

crops.name: Almond
crops.description: Close relative of the peach, with the same early-flowering risk.

crops.name: Alpine Strawberry
crops.description: Tiny intense berries, non-stop, and tolerant of part shade.

crops.name: Amaranth Greens
crops.description: Grown for tender leaves in the heat; the grain type gets much taller.

crops.name: Anise Hyssop
crops.description: Liquorice-scented leaves, purple spikes, adored by pollinators.

crops.name: Apple
crops.description: Most varieties need a second tree nearby to set fruit.

crops.name: Apricot
crops.description: Flowers very early, so a late frost can take the whole crop.

crops.name: Armenian Cucumber
crops.description: Actually a melon; long ribbed fruit that shrugs off heat.

crops.name: Aronia
crops.description: Chokeberry — astringent fresh, excellent cooked, and trouble-free.

crops.name: Arugula
crops.description: Ready in a month, expensive in shops, and peppery enough to matter.

crops.name: Asian Pear
crops.description: Crisp and round, closer to an apple in texture.

crops.name: Asparagus
crops.description: Three years before a real harvest, then twenty more. The longest game here.

crops.name: Avocado
crops.description: Slow, large and frost-sensitive; grafted trees fruit far sooner than seedlings.

crops.name: Banana
crops.description: A giant herb, not a tree. Each stem fruits once and is then cut down.

crops.name: Banana Pepper
crops.description: Mild, tangy and productive; good pickled.

crops.name: Barley
crops.description: Hardier than wheat and quicker off the ground.

crops.name: Basil
crops.description: Absurd value per square foot — supermarket packets are tiny and expensive.

crops.name: Bay Laurel
crops.description: A slow evergreen tree in a pot; a handful of leaves lasts a year.

crops.name: Bee Balm
crops.description: Minty perennial for tea, and hummingbirds find it first.

crops.name: Beefsteak Tomato
crops.description: Big slicing fruit on a heavy vine. Wants the longest, warmest season you have.

crops.name: Beet
crops.description: Two crops in one — roots and the leaves, which are as good as chard.

crops.name: Bell Pepper
crops.description: Sweet peppers ripen from green to red and get sweeter as they do.

crops.name: Bitter Melon
crops.description: Vigorous trellis vine; harvest young for less bitterness.

crops.name: Black Currant
crops.description: Intense flavour and enormous vitamin C.

crops.name: Black-Eyed Peas
crops.description: Heat- and drought-tolerant southern pea.

crops.name: Blackberry
crops.description: Thornless varieties exist and are worth seeking out.

crops.name: Blueberry
crops.description: Needs genuinely acid soil — test first, or grow it in a container.

crops.name: Bok Choy
crops.description: Fast, compact and shade-tolerant — good for a second crop.

crops.name: Borage
crops.description: Cucumber-flavoured leaves and blue flowers bees cannot leave alone.

crops.name: Boysenberry
crops.description: Blackberry-raspberry cross; large soft fruit on trailing canes.

crops.name: Broccoli
crops.description: One main head, then weeks of side shoots if you keep cutting.

crops.name: Broccolini
crops.description: All side shoots, no big head. Longer picking window than broccoli.

crops.name: Brussels Sprouts
crops.description: A long season crop that only gets sweet after frost.

crops.name: Buckwheat
crops.description: Fast cover crop that also makes flour and feeds bees.

crops.name: Bush Beans
crops.description: One concentrated flush, no trellis. Sow a second batch three weeks later.

crops.name: Butterhead Lettuce
crops.description: Soft loose heads, quick to bolt in heat.

crops.name: Butternut Squash
crops.description: Stores for months and tastes better for it.

crops.name: Cabbage
crops.description: One big head per plant; stores for weeks in the cold.

crops.name: Calamondin
crops.description: Sour ornamental citrus that fruits almost continuously indoors.

crops.name: Calendula
crops.description: Petals for salads and salves; flowers until hard frost.

crops.name: Cantaloupe
crops.description: Ready when it slips from the stem and smells like itself.

crops.name: Cardoon
crops.description: Artichoke relative grown for blanched stalks. Architectural and huge.

crops.name: Carrot
crops.description: Wants loose stone-free soil; a raised bed is close to ideal.

crops.name: Cauliflower
crops.description: The fussiest brassica — it wants steady moisture and cool weather throughout.

crops.name: Cayenne
crops.description: Long thin chillies that dry well for flakes and powder.

crops.name: Celeriac
crops.description: Knobbly celery root; long season, worth it for winter soups.

crops.name: Celery
crops.description: Thirsty and slow. Homegrown is darker, stronger and never stringy if watered.

crops.name: Celtuce
crops.description: Grown for a thick crisp stem rather than its leaves.

crops.name: Chamomile
crops.description: Daisy flowers for tea; German chamomile is the annual one.

crops.name: Cherry Tomato
crops.description: Earlier and far more forgiving than a slicer, and it keeps cropping until frost.

crops.name: Chervil
crops.description: Delicate anise notes; prefers shade and cool weather.

crops.name: Chestnut
crops.description: Productive and enormous. Blight-resistant hybrids are the ones to plant.

crops.name: Chia
crops.description: Needs a long frost-free season to ripen seed.

crops.name: Chickpeas
crops.description: Two seeds a pod, so plant more than feels sensible.

crops.name: Chinese Broccoli
crops.description: Gai lan — stems and leaves both, slightly bitter.

crops.name: Chives
crops.description: Perennial, ignores neglect, and flowers are edible too.

crops.name: Cilantro
crops.description: Bolts fast in heat, so sow a little every few weeks rather than all at once.

crops.name: Collard Greens
crops.description: Tougher and more heat-tolerant than kale.

crops.name: Crabapple
crops.description: Grown as a pollinator for other apples; the fruit makes excellent jelly.

crops.name: Cranberry
crops.description: A low acid-loving mat; wants bog conditions, not standing water.

crops.name: Cucumber
crops.description: Climbs happily on a trellis, which keeps the fruit clean and straight.

crops.name: Curry Leaf
crops.description: Tender tree, container-grown outside the tropics.

crops.name: Daikon
crops.description: Large mild winter radish; needs deep soil.

crops.name: Delicata Squash
crops.description: Thin edible skin, sweet flesh, shorter storage than most.

crops.name: Dill
crops.description: Self-seeds readily and draws in beneficial insects.

crops.name: Dwarf Apple
crops.description: Fruits years earlier than a standard tree and stays pickable from the ground.

crops.name: Edamame
crops.description: Soybeans picked green. Harvest the whole plant at once.

crops.name: Eggplant
crops.description: Glossy fruit on a sturdy bush. Wants heat and hates wet feet.

crops.name: Egyptian Walking Onion
crops.description: Sets bulbils on top that flop over and replant themselves.

crops.name: Elderberry
crops.description: Big shrub, big crops, and the raw berries must be cooked.

crops.name: Elephant Garlic
crops.description: Huge mild cloves; botanically closer to a leek.

crops.name: Endive
crops.description: Bitter frilly heads; blanch the centre to soften the flavour.

crops.name: Epazote
crops.description: Pungent Mexican herb cooked with beans.

crops.name: Escarole
crops.description: Broad-leaved endive, better cooked than raw.

crops.name: Fava Beans
crops.description: Sown in cold soil; also fixes nitrogen for whatever follows.

crops.name: Fennel
crops.description: Sweet aniseed bulb; bolts if it dries out or gets warm.

crops.name: Fig
crops.description: Two crops a year in warm climates; cuts back hard and forgives it.

crops.name: Flat-Leaf Parsley
crops.description: Stronger flavour than curly, and easier to chop.

crops.name: Flax
crops.description: Blue-flowered, grown for seed or fibre.

crops.name: Flour Corn
crops.description: Grown to grind, not to eat fresh.

crops.name: Garlic
crops.description: In the ground almost a year, but it asks nothing of you for most of it.

crops.name: Garlic Chives
crops.description: Flat leaves with a mild garlic flavour; spreads if you let it.

crops.name: Ginger
crops.description: Needs warmth, humidity and patience; grows well in a big pot.

crops.name: Globe Artichoke
crops.description: Edible flower buds from a silver thistle. Perennial in mild winters.

crops.name: Goji Berry
crops.description: Arching shrub; needs pruning or it becomes a thicket.

crops.name: Golden Beet
crops.description: Sweeter and milder than red, and it does not stain everything.

crops.name: Gooseberry
crops.description: Tart early fruit on a thorny bush; tolerates some shade.

crops.name: Grain Amaranth
crops.description: Spectacular seed heads, and the young leaves are edible too.

crops.name: Grape
crops.description: Needs a real trellis and annual pruning; then decades of fruit.

crops.name: Grape Tomato
crops.description: Sweet, firm and almost unkillable in a container.

crops.name: Grapefruit
crops.description: Big tree, long ripening, and it wants heat.

crops.name: Green Beans
crops.description: Pole beans crop for weeks from a small footprint. The best use of vertical space.

crops.name: Green Onion
crops.description: Regrows from the base after cutting, so one sowing lasts months.

crops.name: Ground Cherry
crops.description: Sweet husked berries that drop when ripe. Sprawls more than it stands.

crops.name: Guava
crops.description: Fast-growing and heavy-cropping in frost-free gardens.

crops.name: Habanero
crops.description: Fiercely hot and slow to ripen; needs a long warm season.

crops.name: Hardy Kiwi
crops.description: Smooth grape-sized fruit, eaten skin and all, and far more cold tolerant.

crops.name: Hazelnut
crops.description: More a large shrub than a tree; plant two for pollination.

crops.name: Holy Basil
crops.description: Tulsi — grown as much for tea as for cooking.

crops.name: Honeyberry
crops.description: Haskap — the earliest fruit of the year and extremely cold hardy.

crops.name: Honeydew
crops.description: Longer season than a cantaloupe and less forgiving.

crops.name: Hops
crops.description: Climbs twenty feet a season and dies back to the crown each winter.

crops.name: Horseradish
crops.description: Plant it once and you have it forever, whether you want it or not.

crops.name: Iceberg Lettuce
crops.description: Slow and thirsty for what it gives back, but it is what a wedge salad needs.

crops.name: Jalapeño
crops.description: Reliable, compact and hot. One plant covers most households.

crops.name: Japanese Eggplant
crops.description: Slender, thin-skinned and quicker than a globe type.

crops.name: Jicama
crops.description: Crisp sweet root on a long vine. Only the root is edible.

crops.name: Jostaberry
crops.description: Gooseberry-currant cross, thornless and vigorous.

crops.name: Jujube
crops.description: Drought-proof and productive where little else fruits.

crops.name: Kabocha Squash
crops.description: Dense and chestnut-sweet; a sprawling vine.

crops.name: Kale
crops.description: Pick the lower leaves and it keeps going for months, right through frost.

crops.name: Kiwi
crops.description: Vigorous and heavy — the structure matters more than the plant.

crops.name: Kohlrabi
crops.description: Swollen stem above ground, crisp and mild. Pick before it turns woody.

crops.name: Komatsuna
crops.description: Japanese mustard spinach — quick and unfussy.

crops.name: Kumquat
crops.description: Eaten whole, skin and all. The most container-friendly citrus.

crops.name: Lacinato Kale
crops.description: Dark strappy leaves, better texture than curly kale.

crops.name: Lavender
crops.description: Culinary as well as ornamental. Needs sharp drainage and sun.

crops.name: Leek
crops.description: Long season, but it sits happily in frozen ground until you want it.

crops.name: Lemon
crops.description: Crops almost year-round in mild climates and takes to a pot well.

crops.name: Lemon Balm
crops.description: Lemony and perennial; self-seeds everywhere if allowed.

crops.name: Lemon Cucumber
crops.description: Round, pale and mild — easier on the stomach than a slicer.

crops.name: Lemongrass
crops.description: A clumping grass; cut stalks as you need them.

crops.name: Lentils
crops.description: Low yield for the space, but drought-hardy and easy.

crops.name: Lettuce
crops.description: Cut-and-come-again leaves for weeks. The easiest win in a small bed.

crops.name: Lima Beans
crops.description: Needs a long warm season to fill its pods.

crops.name: Lime
crops.description: More cold-tender than lemon; bring it inside where winters bite.

crops.name: Lingonberry
crops.description: Evergreen ground cover with tart red fruit; happy in part shade.

crops.name: Loquat
crops.description: Flowers in winter, fruits in spring; evergreen and handsome.

crops.name: Lovage
crops.description: Tastes like intense celery and returns every year, taller each time.

crops.name: Luffa
crops.description: Eat it young or dry it into a sponge. Needs a very long season.

crops.name: Makrut Lime
crops.description: Grown for its double leaves more than its fruit.

crops.name: Malabar Spinach
crops.description: A climbing heat-lover for when real spinach has bolted.

crops.name: Mandarin
crops.description: Easy-peel, cold-hardiest of the sweet citrus.

crops.name: Mango
crops.description: Needs a genuinely tropical climate or a very large greenhouse.

crops.name: Marigold
crops.description: Planted as much for pest confusion as for the petals.

crops.name: Marjoram
crops.description: Sweeter and gentler than oregano; tender in hard winters.

crops.name: Millet
crops.description: Fast, heat- and drought-tolerant small grain.

crops.name: Mini Sweet Pepper
crops.description: Small sweet peppers in quantity — heavy croppers for their size.

crops.name: Mint
crops.description: Vigorous to the point of invasive. Keep it in a pot, always.

crops.name: Mizuna
crops.description: Feathery mild mustard, cuts and regrows.

crops.name: Mulberry
crops.description: Fruits heavily and young. Plant it well away from paths and cars.

crops.name: Mustard Greens
crops.description: Peppery and fast. Bolts the moment it gets warm.

crops.name: Mâche
crops.description: Corn salad — tiny nutty rosettes that survive real winter.

crops.name: Napa Cabbage
crops.description: Upright barrel-shaped head; the one for kimchi.

crops.name: Nasturtium
crops.description: Leaves, flowers and seed pods all edible and peppery. Trails anywhere.

crops.name: Nectarine
crops.description: A fuzzless peach, with the same habits and the same diseases.

crops.name: New Zealand Spinach
crops.description: Sprawling, salty-sweet and unbothered by summer.

crops.name: Oakleaf Lettuce
crops.description: Lobed tender leaves that stand picking over and over.

crops.name: Oats
crops.description: Easy to grow, tedious to hull.

crops.name: Olive
crops.description: Needs curing before it is edible, and a mild winter to survive.

crops.name: Onion
crops.description: Cheap to buy, but homegrown keeps far longer. Day length decides the variety.

crops.name: Orach
crops.description: Magenta mountain spinach; holds longer than spinach before bolting.

crops.name: Orange
crops.description: Sweet oranges need real summer heat to develop sugar.

crops.name: Oregano
crops.description: Drought-tolerant perennial that gets stronger in poor soil.

crops.name: Padrón
crops.description: Picked small and fried; left on the plant they turn fiery.

crops.name: Papaya
crops.description: Fruits within a year from seed, and dies young.

crops.name: Parsley
crops.description: Slow to start, then productive for a full year in mild climates.

crops.name: Parsnip
crops.description: Slow to germinate, slow to grow, and much sweeter after a frost.

crops.name: Passionfruit
crops.description: Fast tender vine with extraordinary flowers.

crops.name: Pattypan Squash
crops.description: Scalloped little squash; pick them small.

crops.name: Pawpaw
crops.description: North America's largest native fruit — custardy, and it needs shade when young.

crops.name: Peach
crops.description: Fast to fruit, short-lived, and needs annual pruning to stay productive.

crops.name: Peanuts
crops.description: Pegs down into the soil and ripens underground. Needs a long warm season.

crops.name: Pear
crops.description: Longer-lived than apple and just as dependent on a pollinator.

crops.name: Pecan
crops.description: Needs a long hot summer and decades of patience.

crops.name: Peppermint
crops.description: Stronger and cooler than spearmint; spreads just as aggressively.

crops.name: Persimmon
crops.description: Astringent types must go completely soft; fuyu types can be eaten crisp.

crops.name: Pickling Cucumber
crops.description: Short, bumpy fruit bred for jars. Pick every other day.

crops.name: Pineapple
crops.description: One fruit per plant after two years, from a rosette of spiny leaves.

crops.name: Plum
crops.description: Reliable and heavy-cropping; thin the fruit or branches break.

crops.name: Poblano
crops.description: Mild chilli with walls thick enough to stuff and roast.

crops.name: Pomegranate
crops.description: Drought-tolerant and happiest with a long hot summer.

crops.name: Popcorn
crops.description: Left on the stalk to dry hard; stores for years.

crops.name: Potato
crops.description: Cheap to buy, but a good crop in poor soil and forgiving of neglect.

crops.name: Pumpkin
crops.description: Needs real room. Grow it for the season rather than the savings.

crops.name: Purple Carrot
crops.description: Same growing, more money per pound, and it keeps its colour raw.

crops.name: Purslane
crops.description: Succulent, lemony and drought-proof. Often pulled up as a weed.

crops.name: Quince
crops.description: Hard and aromatic; inedible raw, remarkable cooked.

crops.name: Quinoa
crops.description: Needs cool nights to set seed properly.

crops.name: Radicchio
crops.description: Red chicory that only colours up properly in the cold.

crops.name: Radish
crops.description: Four weeks from seed to plate. The fastest thing in the garden.

crops.name: Ramps
crops.description: Wild leeks. Years to establish, and shade is a requirement not a tolerance.

crops.name: Raspberry
crops.description: Spreads by suckers and fruits on canes. Expensive to buy, easy to grow.

crops.name: Red Cabbage
crops.description: Slower than green cabbage and holds its colour when cooked with acid.

crops.name: Red Currant
crops.description: Translucent strings of fruit, heavy crops, very cold hardy.

crops.name: Red Onion
crops.description: Milder than a yellow onion and stores nearly as well.

crops.name: Rhubarb
crops.description: Crops for decades from one crown. Leaves are poisonous, stalks are not.

crops.name: Roma Tomato
crops.description: Dense, low-seed paste tomato — the one to grow if you cook sauce.

crops.name: Romaine
crops.description: Upright crisp hearts; more heat-tolerant than butterhead.

crops.name: Romanesco
crops.description: Fractal lime-green head; grows like a slow cauliflower.

crops.name: Roselle
crops.description: Grown for the tart red calyces that make hibiscus tea.

crops.name: Rosemary
crops.description: Woody evergreen shrub in mild climates; hates wet roots.

crops.name: Runner Beans
crops.description: Tall, scarlet-flowered and edible — the prettiest way to screen a fence.

crops.name: Rutabaga
crops.description: Sweet dense winter keeper. Slower than a turnip.

crops.name: Rye
crops.description: The toughest cereal; often sown to hold soil over winter.

crops.name: Sage
crops.description: Silvery perennial; one plant is more than any kitchen needs.

crops.name: Savoy Cabbage
crops.description: Crinkled leaves, sweeter after a frost.

crops.name: Serrano
crops.description: Hotter and thinner-walled than a jalapeño, and just as easy.

crops.name: Sesame
crops.description: Heat-loving; pods shatter the moment they are ripe.

crops.name: Shallot
crops.description: One planted bulb becomes a cluster. Expensive in shops.

crops.name: Shelling Peas
crops.description: Sweetest within minutes of picking, which is the whole argument for growing them.

crops.name: Shishito
crops.description: Blister them whole. Mostly mild, with the occasional hot surprise.

crops.name: Shiso
crops.description: Perilla — minty, anise-like, and it self-sows freely.

crops.name: Snap Peas
crops.description: Eat pod and all. The first thing worth picking each spring.

crops.name: Snow Peas
crops.description: Flat pods for stir-fries; pick before the peas swell.

crops.name: Sorghum
crops.description: Drought-hardy grain, or a syrup crop from the sweet types.

crops.name: Sorrel
crops.description: Sharp lemony leaves from a plant that comes back each year.

crops.name: Sour Cherry
crops.description: Smaller, self-fertile and far easier than a sweet cherry.

crops.name: Spaghetti Squash
crops.description: Flesh pulls into strands when roasted.

crops.name: Spearmint
crops.description: The mint for tea and tabbouleh. Contain the roots.

crops.name: Spinach
crops.description: Fast, cold-hardy and expensive to buy — one of the best value crops there is.

crops.name: Squash Blossom
crops.description: The male flowers of any summer squash, picked before they set fruit.

crops.name: Stevia
crops.description: Leaves are intensely sweet fresh or dried.

crops.name: Strawberry
crops.description: Everbearing types fruit through the season. Runners give you free plants.

crops.name: Sugar Pumpkin
crops.description: Small pie pumpkin — actually worth cooking, unlike the big carving sort.

crops.name: Summer Savory
crops.description: Peppery and traditional with beans.

crops.name: Sunchoke
crops.description: Jerusalem artichoke — enormous, unkillable, and it will spread.

crops.name: Sunflower
crops.description: Seeds for you or the birds, and shade for whatever needs it.

crops.name: Sweet Cherry
crops.description: You will be sharing it with birds unless you net it.

crops.name: Sweet Corn
crops.description: Plant in a block, not a row, or the ears fill unevenly. Sweetest straight off the stalk.

crops.name: Sweet Onion
crops.description: Low-sulphur and juicy; poor keeper, eat it first.

crops.name: Sweet Potato
crops.description: Sprawling vines, heat-loving, and the leaves are edible too.

crops.name: Swiss Chard
crops.description: Harvest outer stalks all season. Handles both heat and frost.

crops.name: Tarragon
crops.description: French tarragon has to be grown from division, not seed.

crops.name: Tatsoi
crops.description: Flat spoon-leaved rosette; very cold hardy.

crops.name: Tayberry
crops.description: Aromatic and sharp; too soft to travel, which is why shops rarely have it.

crops.name: Thai Basil
crops.description: Anise-scented and sturdier in heat than sweet basil.

crops.name: Thai Chilli
crops.description: Tiny, very hot, and ornamental enough for a patio pot.

crops.name: Thyme
crops.description: Tiny leaves, huge shelf price, and it thrives on being ignored.

crops.name: Tomatillo
crops.description: Husked fruit for salsa verde. Plant two — a lone plant sets almost nothing.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.description: High-value staple that anchors most household gardens. Needs staking and steady water.

crops.name: Turmeric
crops.description: Same conditions as ginger, and the same very long wait.

crops.name: Turnip
crops.description: Roots and tops both usable; best picked small.

crops.name: Turnip Greens
crops.description: Grown for the tops rather than the root.

crops.name: Viola
crops.description: Candied or scattered on a plate; happiest in cool weather.

crops.name: Walnut
crops.description: Huge, long-lived, and it poisons many plants beneath it.

crops.name: Watercress
crops.description: Wants constantly wet roots; happiest in a tray of water.

crops.name: Watermelon
crops.description: Wants heat, room and patience. Thin to two fruit per vine.

crops.name: Watermelon Radish
crops.description: Green outside, magenta in. Slower and milder than a breakfast radish.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.description: A garden-scale patch yields a loaf or two — grown for interest more than value.

crops.name: White Currant
crops.description: Sweeter and milder than red; the same plant otherwise.

crops.name: Yacon
crops.description: Sweet crunchy tubers that taste closer to fruit than potato.

crops.name: Yardlong Beans
crops.description: Thrives in heat that stops ordinary beans.

crops.name: Yellow Squash
crops.description: Crookneck summer squash, as prolific as zucchini.

crops.name: Zucchini
crops.description: Absurdly productive. Two plants will feed a street.
